findings.remediation: Use persist-credentials: false when checking out external/untrusted repositories.
findings.impact: An untrusted checkout can read a persisted GITHUB_TOKEN from Git configuration and reuse its repository privileges.
findings.attack_vector: actions/checkout selects an external or event-controlled revision while persist-credentials remains enabled.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: workflow downloads remote scripts without integrity verification
findings.remediation: Add checksum/GPG verification for all downloaded artifacts.
findings.impact: Downloading scripts without integrity verification allows MITM substitution of malicious code.
findings.attack_vector: curl/wget in workflow without checksum/sha256 verification — attacker intercepts and replaces.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: sensitive GitHub token permissions: contents:write, id-token:write, attestations:write, pull-requests:write
findings.remediation: Grant write scopes only to the job that needs them and keep all other scopes read-only or none.
findings.impact: A compromised workflow step can modify repository content, packages, deployments, checks, or security records within the granted scope.
findings.attack_vector: A permissions block grants a named write scope; exploitability depends on whether untrusted code reaches that job.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.
